chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Jamīl ibn Ṣāliḥ, from al-Fuḍayl ibn Yasār, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man whose marriage contract is in place and who performed ẓihār regarding his wife,
So he said: “There is no ẓihār, and there is no īlāʾ, until he consummates the marriage with her.”

key_terms.إِيلَاءٌ: an oath of abstention from marital relations
key_terms.ظَاهَرَ: he declared ẓihār against his wife
key_terms.ظِهَارٌ: the legal formula likening one's wife to a prohibited relative
key_terms.مُمْلَكٍ: a man with a contracted marriage, before consummation
key_terms.يَدْخُلَ بِهَا: he consummates the marriage with her

ai.seo_question: Does ẓihār or īlāʾ apply before consummation of marriage in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that ẓihār and īlāʾ do not take effect before consummation of the marriage. It clarifies a condition in family law concerning the legal validity of these forms of marital declaration.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.4826 - Al-Hasan bin Mahbub narrated from Jamil bin Salih, from Al-Fudayl bin Yasar, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who has only performed the marriage contract (mamluk, meaning he has not yet consummated the marriage) and then declares ẓihar (a pre-Islamic form of divorce where a husband likens his wife to a prohibited relative).
Imam (as) said: "There is no ẓihar and no īla' (an oath to abstain from marital relations) until he consummates the marriage with her."
